stages.sub: How reliance on raw materials shapes the trade and development strategies a poor country can pursue.

steps.q: A country earns most of its export income from selling raw cocoa and copper ore, not phones or cars. If world cocoa and copper prices crash one year, what happens to the country's export income?
steps.hint: If nearly all your exports are these two goods, what happens when their prices fall together?

steps.q: Because this country's income depends so heavily on just cocoa and copper prices, does that income stay steady from year to year?
steps.right: No, it swings with world prices
steps.wrong: Yes, it stays steady each year
steps.hint: World prices for raw materials move a lot. What does that do to the money coming in?

steps.q: A new domestic car factory cannot yet make cars as cheaply as huge, experienced foreign car firms. If tariffs shield it from foreign competition for a few years while it learns and grows, could it eventually become efficient enough to compete without protection?
steps.hint: Think about why the factory struggles now: is it because it can never be efficient, or because it hasn't had the chance to grow yet?
